sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Show single-table" button to multi-table relationship/performance sub-sections (artist-relationships, label-relationships, place-performances) that have no MusicBrainz overflow (i.e. every row is already rendered, ≤100). Clicking it opens the currently-rendered rows as a standalone single-table view in a new browser tab via a client-side snapshot handoff (GM_setValue/GM_getValue keyed by a per-click uid, plus a `#mb-sa-snapshot=<uid>` hash marker on a `?link_type_id=1`-qualified URL) — no MusicBrainz re-fetch, unlike the existing native-overflow "Show all N rows" button. New settings: sa_ui_show_single_table_btn_bg / sa_ui_show_single_table_btn_bg_clicked.

Extended the "Show single-table" button to artist-releasegroups (e.g. an artist's bare overview page) and releasegroup-releases sub-sections, whose categories never carry a MusicBrainz overflow link at all (unlike relationships/performances, these page types accumulate every row themselves via their own multi-page fetch, so MB never imposes a per-category cap to begin with). These page types have no "-filtered" single-table sibling definition to route to via a query-param trick, so the new tab reuses the bare multi-mode URL as-is — MusicBrainz's own native table on that page already carries class="tbl" for the existing hydrate/fallback-fabrication logic to hook into. The button-eligibility whitelist and the link_type_id-routing decision are now centralized in two Sets (SA_SNAPSHOT_SUPPORTED_PAGETYPES, SA_SNAPSHOT_LINK_TYPE_ID_PAGETYPES) instead of duplicated inline conditions.

Extracted loadTableDataFromDisk()'s render/reconstruction body into a shared _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData(data, opts) function, reused by both the existing "Load from Disk" feature and the new cross-tab snapshot bootstrap, so both consumers get identical row reconstruction, render, and post-render wiring instead of two independently drifting implementations. Also hardened it with a fallback that fabricates an empty table.tbl shell when none exists natively on the page (benefits any future caller lacking a live table, not just the snapshot handoff).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a "Cannot access '_filterResultCache' before initialization" crash when opening a "Show single-table" snapshot tab: the hash-marker bootstrap hook ran mid-way through the script's initial synchronous top-to-bottom execution, calling into _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData() (via runFilter()/_invalidateFilterCache()) before later module-level const/let bindings in the same top-level scope had initialized. Every other caller (a button click, a FileReader.onload) only ever fires after the whole script has finished its first synchronous pass; the bootstrap's hydrate call is now deferred one tick via setTimeout(...,0) to match.

Fixed the snapshot tab's <h2> heading always showing MusicBrainz's own native label for whichever relationship/performance type the placeholder `?link_type_id=1` happens to resolve to (e.g. "next disc" relationships) instead of the actually-captured category (e.g. "Produced release"). Added _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel(), called after hydration settles, to replace just the bare heading text node with the real category name.

Fixed inline CAA thumbnails and sticky-column not working for release/release-group snapshot tabs: reconstructed headers carried leftover uniq-value count-badge digits (e.g. "Title" -> "Title 18") baked into their captured innerHTML, which makeTableSortableUnified's colName derivation absorbed into dataset.colName (it deliberately does not strip plain 0-9, to avoid mangling genuine numeric column names like "1st seconder"), breaking every name-based column lookup downstream (caaFindColumnByName, applyStickyColumn). The header-restore step in _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData now collapses an already-decorated .mb-col-hdr-flex header back to its clean name text before makeTableSortableUnified re-processes it — a general fix that also corrects the same latent bug in the existing "Load from Disk" feature.

Fixed _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() correcting the wrong <h2> on busy pages (e.g. a release-group's bare overview, which has its own Wikipedia-extract h2 ahead of the Releases one): it now walks all h2s to find the one that actually immediately precedes table.tbl in document order (mirrors updateH2Count()'s own targetH2 resolution), instead of naively grabbing the first h2.mb-toggle-h2 on the page.

Investigated a reload race on artist-releasegroups/releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs, where a separately-installed third-party userscript (a Picard/Tagger-port integration script) auto-reloads the bare entity page shortly after load to append its own query param, wiping out the hydrated snapshot — confirmed via HAR network-log initiator trace to be that script's own reloadWithTaggerPort(), not this script's code. Added a stopOtherScripts() call (the same window.stopAllUserScripts + 'mb-stop-all-scripts' signal startFetchingProcess() already sends before every normal fetch) as early as possible in the hash-marker bootstrap, on the chance a cooperating script checks it — confirmed by testing that this specific third-party script does NOT check it, so the race remains for anyone running it alongside this one. Not fixable from here: cooperation from an independently-installed script can't be forced. Workaround: disable/adjust that script for this workflow, or use the browser's Stop button before the reload completes.

Fixed "Show single-table" on artist-releasegroups showing multiple h3-based subtables still native/unprocessed in the new tab: MusicBrainz's own artist-overview page already groups release-groups into several separate native `<h3>` + `<table class="tbl release-group-list mergeable-table">` sections (one per release-group type), and the header-restore step only ever targeted the FIRST table.tbl found, leaving the rest fully native alongside the hydrated single-table view. Added _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot(), called before every snapshot hydration, which removes all such h3+table.tbl sections first (only acting on an h3 when a table.tbl is actually found in its sibling chain, so unrelated h3s — e.g. from other installed userscripts — are left alone) so the existing "no table.tbl found — fabricate a fresh shell" fallback always builds exactly one, correctly-scoped table.

Fixed _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() stealing a release-group's native "Relationships" section heading on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs (e.g. relabeling it to “Bootleg release” releases, with the Relationships section's own original content — e.g. its "associated singles/EPs:"/"other databases:" rows — then visibly dangling right after it): _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot only ever clears h3+table.tbl "Releases" sections by design, so the Relationships h2 section survives, and once the fabricated table lands past that surviving section, "the h2 immediately preceding table.tbl" resolves to it instead of anything Releases-related. The "no table.tbl found" fabrication branch now creates its own dedicated `<h2>` (stamped `data-mb-sa-fabricated-heading`) and positions the fabricated table right after it — nothing native can ever land between them again — and _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() targets that marker directly instead of guessing via document order. The nearest-preceding-h2 heuristic remains as a fallback for the three pageTypes that reuse an existing native table.tbl (routed via ?link_type_id=1) rather than fabricating one.

Fixed two more releasegroup-releases snapshot-tab bugs — a `<td class="relationships">` (with a discogs favicon link) appended as literally every row's 2nd cell right after the sticky column, and every release's cover-art image doubled in the big-picture stripe above the table — both traced to the separately-installed jesus2099 "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript (already known to this codebase via its `'jesus2099'` columnEraser, its bigbox cleanup in performClutterCleanup(), and initTreleasesObserver()'s handling of its injected `<tr class="treleases">` rows). That script reacts to the page on its own schedule; the normal fetch-and-render flow's one-shot cleanup is timed after it has already run, but the snapshot-hydrate bootstrap replaces the page within one setTimeout(...,0) tick of the tab opening, so jesus2099's own injection can still be pending — it then injects its favicon-link column and a second `div.jesus2099userjs154481bigbox` into whichever rows/table it finds moments later, which are now this script's freshly-hydrated ones. Added _watchForLateJesus2099Injections(), a short-lived (5s) MutationObserver installed at the very start of the snapshot bootstrap that strips both as soon as they appear, mirroring initTreleasesObserver()'s existing childList+attributes pattern.

Fixed the jesus2099 "relationships" <td> race fix (WIP.1 above) leaving its HEADER-side twin behind: a bare `<th>Relationships</th>` (no class, no data-col-name, none of this script's own header-marker classes) landed as the table's 2nd header on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs, right after "Release" — jesus2099 injects a whole column (one header cell, one data cell per row), and cleanupHeaders() only strips a header matching that text once, right after renderFinalTable(), before jesus2099's late injection lands on this fast bootstrap path. _watchForLateJesus2099Injections() now also matches and removes any bare foreign <th> whose text starts with "Relationships"/"Performance Attributes"/"Release events"/"Tagger" (cleanupHeaders()'s own removalMapAlways list) and carries none of this script's own header classes.

Fixed (root cause confirmed via debug logging added in the previous attempt) a release-group's native "Album" h2 (the one wrapping the Official/Promotion/Bootleg release h3+table sections) surviving on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs as an empty, collapsed, count-less stub once _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot cleared every h3+table pair beneath it. A structural analysis of an earlier debug HTML capture showed "Album" owning exactly 3 h3s, all removable — but the debug log from a live reproduction showed "h2 'Album' owns no h3" and "Cleared 1 pre-existing native table.tbl section(s) (0 h3-anchored, …)": this whole bootstrap runs within one setTimeout(...,0) tick of the tab opening — fast enough to beat MusicBrainz's OWN client-side JS splitting the release listing into its Official/Promotion/Bootleg h3 subsections, so at the moment this function actually ran, "Album" still owned a single flat table.tbl directly (no h3 wrapping yet), which the unconditional "remainingTables" sweep silently absorbed — leaving "Album" itself unaccounted for by the h3-only ownership check. _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot now also records, in the same up-front walk, which table.tbl each h2 owns DIRECTLY (no h3 in between), and treats that exactly like an owned-and-removed h3 for emptiness purposes.

Fixed the fabricated heading (see the "stealing a native Relationships heading" fix above) being inserted directly after `

`, which pushed MusicBrainz's own native `

` ("~Release group by …") and `

` (Overview/Aliases/Tags/Reviews/Details/Edit) down BELOW the fabricated heading and table on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs — that page-level chrome belongs directly under h1, not sandwiched below new content. The fabrication branch now anchors after the LAST `div.tabs` instead (the same preference order applyInsertH2 already uses for this exact problem), falling back to right after h1 only when no tabs bar exists at all.

Fixed a leftover MusicBrainz native `<h2>` (e.g. "next disc" relationships) plus its "No relationships of the selected type were found." paragraph appearing ABOVE the correctly-labeled fabricated section on artist-relationships/label-relationships/place-performances snapshot tabs, whenever the `?link_type_id=1` placeholder genuinely has zero native matches. When a native table.tbl DOES exist for the placeholder, _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel already just relabels that table's own h2 in place (no duplicate) — but with zero matches there is no native table at all, so the "no table.tbl found" branch fabricates a brand new heading+table instead of reusing the native one, leaving the old native placeholder heading and its "not found" message behind as unrelated noise. The fabrication branch now removes that native placeholder h2 (and its content, up to the next h2) first, for the 3 pageTypes routed via ?link_type_id=1, before inserting its own dedicated heading at the same anchor point.
